documented_range.note: The shore of Mitchell's 1870 map; the scene's phase begins in 1860.

change_note: Built T-3689 (2026-11-20): the lake shore refuge, on the landmark_1871 archetype.

placement.position_note: Along the 1871 plan's shore line from (845.06, 2703.29) to (638.19, 3392.44) (data/context/1871/plan.json, from Mitchell's 1870 map), on the level ground 16 to 40 m inland of the plan's line, above the bank. The footprint's origin is local E 818.24 N 2695.24.

fire.note: Open sand: nothing on it to burn.

value.note: THE LAKE SHORE SANDS by the old City Cemetery and Lincoln Park, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: the open shore where the people of the North Side fled from the fire on Monday 9 October 1871. Refugees were 'at Lincoln Park and the old cemetery to the south of it, and along the Lake-shore Drive' (Colbert and Chamberlin, p. 265); 'along the beach were judges, merchants, doctors, workingmen, women and children' (Sheahan and Upton, pp. 113-114). The strip follows the 1871 plan's shore line (Mitchell's 1870 map) along the cemetery; how wide the sand ran is reconstructed.

composition.note: A level strip of sand; reconstructed.

kind.note: An open beach (Sheahan and Upton, pp. 113-114): the walker reads it and lets the visitor walk on it; nothing in the mesh comes from it.

function.note: The beach along the North Side (Sheahan and Upton, pp. 113-114).

built.note: Natural shore; the year only opens the record.

citations.citation: Elias Colbert and Everett Chamberlin, Chicago and the Great Conflagration. Cincinnati and New York: C. F. Vent; Chicago: J. S. Goodman & Co., 1871.
what_it_supplies: A citywide ratio of building materials before the fire: in spring 1868, 35,654 wooden buildings to 3,712 of brick and stone (about nine in ten wooden).
The city's 59,500 buildings in 1871 by division, with the West Division largest (29,400).
Descriptions that the West Side's burned blocks were nearly all frame, and that the South Division's burned centre held the city's most expensive structures.
what_it_does_not_supply: A material for any particular lot, block or street; a material ratio by division or for 1871 itself; paint colours.

citations.citation: S. Augustus Mitchell, Jr. Chicago. 1870. Approximately 1:31,000. University of Illinois Map and Geography Library; Wikimedia Commons surrogate.
what_it_supplies: Named streets and diagonals, river courses, lake edge, lakefront railroad and lagoon relationships, rail corridors and named parks.
Coverage from Fullerton Avenue to Thirty-first Street and Western Avenue to Lake Michigan.
what_it_does_not_supply: Individual building footprints, occupants, exact paving, engineered widths or elevations.
The western extension to Fortieth Avenue or southern continuation to Egan Avenue; these require separate evidence and reconstructed geometry.

citations.citation: Sheahan, James W., and George P. Upton. The Great Conflagration. Chicago: Its Past, Present and Future. Philadelphia: Union Publishing Co., 1871.
what_it_supplies: the authors' count of the people made homeless by the fire of October 1871: 98,860
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about the buildings of 1812 or 1835: the town those scenes show was gone long before 1871
